title: Rental, occupancy & HOA rules
disclaimer: Not legal advice — rules change; check the official source.
notes: Values are short summaries in our own words, not quotations. Follow the source link before relying on any of them.
verified: true = read on an official page this session; "partial" = part read, part from news or a docket; false = from background knowledge or a search snippet.
Model codes (IPMC, IRC) are copyrighted by the ICC: we link to them and do not quote them.
2026-11-24: second-pass verification against official code hosts, statutes and agency pages; 'evidence' names the section relied on.

deposit.value: No statutory cap on amount. Return within three weeks after tenancy ends (5 days if condemned) with 1% simple annual interest, or give a written statement of amounts withheld.
deposit.evidence: 504B.178 subd. 2 (1% simple interest) and subd. 3 (three weeks, written statement); section sets no amount limit.

notice.value: Tenancy at will: written notice at least as long as the rent interval or three months, whichever is less (504B.135). Fixed-term and periodic leases follow their lease terms.
notice.evidence: 504B.135 Terminating tenancy at will: rent interval or three months, whichever less, in writing.

hoa_law.value: Common Interest Ownership Act (ch. 515B); association must keep records available to owners (515B.3-118). Flag bans void (500.215); solar limits restricted (500.216); child-care bans restricted (500.217). Use/occupancy (incl. leasing) restrictions must be in the declaration (515B.2-105(a)(11)).

yigby.value: SF 4915 (YIGBY Housing Act), companion HF 5020: introduced 3/26/2026, referred to Senate State and Local Government, no further action. Not law. Church-land housing needs normal zoning approval.
yigby.evidence: Spot-check: bill status shows introduction 3/26/2026 and committee referral only.

rluipa.value: Federal law: zoning may not substantially burden religious exercise without a compelling reason, must treat religious assemblies on equal terms with secular ones, and may not exclude them outright.
rluipa.evidence: Federal field already verified; not re-read in this MN lane.

worship_zoning.value: Religious place of assembly is a permitted use in nearly all districts (Table 545-1). Minneapolis code has no sacred-community rule, so under Minn. Stat. 327.30 micro-unit villages at a church's main worship site must be approved as a conditional use. Other housing on church land needs normal approval.
worship_zoning.evidence: Table 545-1 Religious place of assembly row; code search found no sacred-community text; 327.30 subd. 3(c).

shed.value: A shed is not a dwelling unit: a unit needs its own kitchen, sleeping area and bathroom for one household. Living space in an accessory building is legal only as a detached ADU meeting Ch. 550 Art. IX. Temporary structures used for living are banned (244.60).
shed.evidence: 565 definition of Dwelling unit; 550.1420-.1430 ADU rules; 244.60 temporary housing prohibited.

tent.value: Banned: no tent or other temporary structure may be placed on public or private property and used for living (244.60). The regulatory services director may permit temporary housing only for specified emergencies such as natural disasters or public-health emergencies.
tent.evidence: Sec. 244.60 Temporary housing prohibited; exception for emergency permits.

rv.value: Banned: no camp car, house trailer, automobile or similar may be parked on a street or private premises and used for living (244.60), except under an emergency permit. A proposed Safe Outdoor Parking amendment would allow managed overnight vehicle-sleeping lots by interim use permit.
rv.evidence: Sec. 244.60 Temporary housing prohibited; city Safe Outdoor Parking amendment page (pending).

thow.value: Not a dwelling: transportable structures not permanently attached count as temporary housing, which 244.60 bans for living. Exception: state law (327.30) lets churches host micro units on a chassis for chronically homeless and low-income people as a conditional use.
thow.evidence: 244.10 definition of Temporary housing; 244.60; Minn. Stat. 327.30 subd. 3(c) and subd. 4.

rooming.value: Rooming houses not otherwise defined are an example of a prohibited use (545.80). Rooming units are allowed only through congregate living uses such as nonprofit- or agency-run single room occupancy housing (permitted in most districts). Housing code treats a rooming house as a licensed lodging establishment.
rooming.evidence: 545.80 Prohibited uses item 5; Table 545-1 congregate living rows; 565 Rooming unit; 244.10 Rooming house.

coliving.value: Two or more unrelated adults can count as one family if they operate as a registered intentional community (244.820). Intentional community is a permitted use in most districts. Limits: units let to separate roomers do not qualify, and a rental owner may have only one intentional-community dwelling (nonprofits and owner-cooperatives exempt).
coliving.evidence: Sec. 244.820(c)-(d) intentional community; Table 545-1 Intentional community row.

per_bedroom.value: Sleeping rooms need 70 sq ft for 1 person, 90 for 2, plus 50 for each extra person, and at most 4 people per sleeping room. Multi-use habitable rooms need 150 sq ft and other habitable rooms 70 (Housing Maintenance Code 244.810).
per_bedroom.evidence: Sec. 244.810 Required space in dwelling units, sleeping-room floor areas and four-person cap.

permit.value: Yes: licence for stays of 30 days or fewer. Renting a spare room while the host stays home is exempt.
permit.evidence: Spot-check: city STR page, Who needs this license and Exemptions sections.

primary_residence.value: No, but an owner (LLCs included) may hold only one STR licence besides their home; non-homestead units must submit management and floor plans.
primary_residence.evidence: City STR page: one STR property besides home; non-homestead rows of requirements table.

zones.value: Short-term rental units count as dwelling units under zoning and are licensed under Ch. 351, so they go wherever dwellings are allowed. Hotels and hostels (5-20 rooms) are a separate lodging use, limited to certain districts.
zones.evidence: 545 Lodging use category exception 2 (STR units are dwelling units, Ch. 351); Table 545-1 lodging rows.

caps.value: 1 non-homestead STR licence per owner; in buildings of 20+ units at most 10% may be STRs (not applied to condo buildings).
caps.evidence: City STR page: 20 or more units, 10 percent; condo exception.

max_occupancy.evidence: City STR page requirements table: limit occupants to 10.

hostel_shared.value: STR licence exempts room rental only when host stays home. Renting sleeping rooms to 5+ people for a week or more needs a city lodging facility licence; per-bed nightly rental not addressed.
hostel_shared.evidence: STR page exemption plus Lodging Facilities licence definition (5+ beds, week or more).

taxes.value: Combined sales tax 9.025% (6.875% state plus local) plus 3% Minneapolis entertainment tax on all short-term lodging; Minneapolis lodging tax only for 50+ room establishments. Facilitating platforms collect.
taxes.evidence: MN DOR Fact Sheet 164M lodging section; DOR metro rate guide Q4 2026; DOR residential STR guide.

listing_id.value: Yes, licence ID must be on the platform listing; licence number serves as registration number, exempt rooms state the exemption.
listing_id.evidence: Spot-check: city STR requirements table and Registration numbers section.

pending.value: Zoning amendments under review: Housing with 1-3 Units (council vote scheduled Dec 3, 2026) and Safe Outdoor Parking (vehicle-sleeping sites). No pending STR licence change found.
pending.evidence: City Proposed and Adopted Amendments page and the two amendment pages' adoption schedules.

registration.value: Every non-owner-occupied unit needs a city rental licence; buildings tiered 1/1D/2/3 by violations, setting inspection cycle (1-8 years) and fees. Active licence data on Open Data Minneapolis is updated weekly.
registration.evidence: City Rental license rules, Tiers, and Active rental licenses pages (data updated weekly).

family.value: No fixed count of unrelated people. Zoning uses the Ch. 244 definition: one or more people living together as a single household for 30+ days, not short-term or transient use. One family per unit (244.820), with room size setting the cap (244.810).
family.evidence: 565 Family refers to Ch. 244; 244.10 Family definition; 244.820 one family per unit.

adu.value: One internal, attached or detached ADU per lot, only accessory to a single- or two-family dwelling, and no separate tax parcel (550.1420-.1430). Single-, two- and three-family dwellings are permitted in the urban-neighborhood districts (Table 545-1). A 1-3 unit code update is pending.
adu.evidence: 550.1420 Permitted ADUs; 550.1430 standards (1) one per lot; Table 545-1 Dwellings rows.

hoa_data.value: No HOA layer for Hennepin. Proxies: MN subdivision plats; Mapping Prejudice historic racial covenants (CC0, history only). Neighborhoods are not HOAs.
hoa_data.evidence: Data-source field, not legal text; not re-checked in this lane.

worship_zoning.value: Religious institutions are permitted in all residential and traditional-neighborhood districts (Tables 66.221, 66.321). Micro-unit dwellings at a religious institution under Minn. Stat. 327.30 are permitted in all residential districts (65.919), and emergency housing at a church is allowed in several districts (65.154).
worship_zoning.evidence: Table 66.221 Religious institution and Micro-unit rows; 65.919 standards; 65.154 Emergency housing facility.

shed.value: Not a dwelling: a dwelling unit needs complete living facilities incl. kitchen and bathroom (60.205). Accessory buildings are limited (63.501); living space there is legal only as a code-compliant ADU (65.913). No explicit shed-occupancy ban section found.
shed.evidence: 60.205 Dwelling unit; 63.501 Accessory buildings; 65.913 ADU. No explicit prohibition text located.

tent.value: No zoning use allows tents as housing; dwelling units need complete facilities (60.205). Tents or membrane structures over 200 sq ft need a fire-code permit (55.04). No explicit anti-camping housing section was found in the code search.
tent.evidence: 60.205 Dwelling unit; 55.04 tent permit; code search for camping/tents found no housing rule.

rv.value: RVs are not dwelling units (60.205 requires complete permanent facilities). Trailers and campers may not be left on streets or alleys unless hitched to a vehicle (157.11). No explicit ban on living in an RV on private land was found.
rv.evidence: 60.205 Dwelling unit; 157.11 Parking for larger vehicles; code search found no RV-occupancy rule.

thow.value: Not a dwelling unit in general. Exception: micro-unit dwellings on a chassis (max 400 sq ft, ANSI 119.5) at a religious institution's main worship site for chronically homeless and low-income residents are permitted in residential districts (65.919, Minn. Stat. 327.30).
thow.evidence: 65.919 Micro-unit dwellings accessory to a religious institution; Minn. Stat. 327.30 subd. 4.

rooming.value: Roominghouse = rooms rented to more than 6 adults by the room (65.158). Conditional use in RM1-RM3 residential districts, with lot area 5,000 sq ft plus 1,000 per guest room over 6; rooming units must have 70 sq ft for 1 person and 60 per person if shared (34.17).
rooming.evidence: 65.158 Roominghouse definition and standards; Table 66.221 row; 34.17(2) floor area.

coliving.value: Up to 6 adults plus their minor children are one household (60.209), so most co-living fits in a dwelling. Larger room-by-room setups are roominghouses (65.158). 'Shareable housing' for collaborative living (65.159) is a permitted use in traditional-neighborhood districts.
coliving.evidence: 60.209 Household; 65.158 Roominghouse; 65.159 Shareable housing; Table 66.321 row.

per_bedroom.value: Dwelling units need 150 sq ft of habitable area for the first occupant and 100 for each additional one. Sleeping rooms need 70 sq ft for 1, or 50 per occupant if shared (34.13). Rooming units need 70 for 1, or 60 per occupant (34.17).
per_bedroom.evidence: Sec. 34.13 Occupancy on residential properties (2)-(3); 34.17(2) rooming units.

permit.value: Yes: annual host licence and platform licence for stays under 30 days (Leg. Code Ch. 379).
permit.evidence: Spot-check: city STR page, less than thirty days; hosts and platforms licensed, renewed annually.

primary_residence.value: No primary-residence rule; owner-occupancy changes how many units may be STRs and whether a Fire C of O is needed.
primary_residence.evidence: City STR requirements table, owner-occupied vs non-owner-occupied rows.

zones.value: Short-term rental dwelling units are P/C (permitted with standards) across residential, traditional-neighborhood and business district tables; per-building counts depend on owner-occupancy and the conditional use permit rules in the STR standards.
zones.evidence: Tables 66.221/66.321 Short term rental dwelling unit rows; STR zoning ordinance districts list.

caps.value: Non-owner-occupied 1-3 unit buildings: 1 STR; non-owner fourplex 1 (RL-RT1) or 2; owner-occupied: all units up to 4; 5+ unit buildings: 50% up to 4. More by conditional use permit.
caps.evidence: City STR requirements table and conditional use permit footnote.

max_occupancy.value: Occupancy capped at the zoning 'family' definition (Sec. 60.207) for one housekeeping unit; more only by conditional use permit for large 1-2 family homes on large lots, 1,000 ft apart.
max_occupancy.evidence: STR zoning ordinance condition (d) on total occupancy; city table footnote.

hostel_shared.value: Portions of a dwelling may be STRs, but occupancy is capped at the family definition; commercial and social events are banned. Per-bed rental not addressed.
hostel_shared.evidence: STR zoning ordinance conditions; city STR page definition.

taxes.value: Combined sales tax 9.875% (6.875% state, 1.5% city, 0.5% Ramsey transit, 1% metro) plus Saint Paul lodging tax 3% (<50 rooms) or 7% (50+). Facilitating platforms collect.
taxes.evidence: MN DOR Special Local Taxes fact sheet, St. Paul entry; DOR metro rate guide Q4 2026.

listing_id.value: Yes: platforms must show the host's licence number on the listing and serve only licensed hosts.
listing_id.evidence: Ord 17-49 (Ch. 379), Sec. 379.06 platform provisions on licensed hosts and licence number on listing.

pending.value: No pending STR change found. Long-term: voter-approved rent stabilization (2021; amended 2022 and 2025) caps increases at 3% per 12 months, with exceptions.
pending.evidence: City Rent Stabilization page overview; no full pending-legislation search.

registration.value: Non-owner-occupied rentals need a Fire Certificate of Occupancy with inspections.
registration.evidence: City STR table requires Fire C of O for non-owner-occupied units; long-term C of O program text not read.

family.value: Zoning 'family' means household: 6 or fewer adults plus minor children in their care, living together in a dwelling unit (60.209). This also caps STR and ADU occupancy. Ch. 40 (Fire C of O) separately defines family as related people plus at most 2 unrelated.
family.evidence: 60.207 Family refers to Household; 60.209 Household definition; 40.03 Family definition.

adu.value: Up to 2 ADUs per one-family dwelling, at least one detached unless 50%+ of the existing house is kept; max 800 sq ft or 75% of the main unit; total occupancy within the household cap; not sold separately (65.913). Permitted in RL-RM2 (Table 66.221). Amended 2018, 2021, 2022 and 2023.
adu.evidence: 65.913 Dwelling unit, accessory (a)-(g) and history notes; Table 66.221 row.

hoa_data.value: No HOA layer for Ramsey; subdivision plat polygons only (no HOA field). District councils are not HOAs.
hoa_data.evidence: Data-source field already verified; not re-checked in this lane.

deposit.value: No statutory cap on amount; landlord must refund on or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the premises (Prop. Code 92.103).
deposit.evidence: Prop. Code 92.103(a): refund due by 30th day after surrender; no amount limit in Subch. C.

notice.value: Month-to-month: tenancy ends the later of the date in the notice or one month after notice; shorter rent periods use that period. A signed lease may set a different notice (Prop. Code 91.001).
notice.evidence: Prop. Code 91.001(a)-(e): one-month rule for monthly tenancies; lease can override.

hoa_law.value: Prop. Code ch. 209: certified-mail notice and cure before fines or suits (209.006), records access (209.005), open board meetings (209.0051), management certificate filed with county and TREC (209.004). Ch. 202 protects solar (202.010), rain barrels and drought landscaping (202.007), wind/hail-resistant shingles (202.011), flags (202.012), religious items (202.018), generators (202.019). Tarr (Tex. 2018) sided with owner on STR.
hoa_law.evidence: Read 202.007, 202.011, ch.202/209 headings, 209.004(b-1), 209.006; Tarr docket 16-1005: 5/25/2018 reversed for owner (opinion not read).

yigby.value: SB 854 (by-right housing on religious land) died in 2025. SB 840 (by-right multifamily on commercial land, from 1 Sep 2025) is the usable route.

rluipa.value: Federal law: zoning may not substantially burden religious exercise without a compelling reason, must treat religious assemblies on equal terms with secular ones, and may not exclude them outright.

worship_zoning.value: Church use is permitted by right in all residential and nonresidential districts except P(A) (Dev. Code 51A-4.204(4)). Housing on church land still needs a residential use allowed in that district.
worship_zoning.evidence: 51A-4.204(4) Church: by right in all districts except P(A).

shed.value: No dwelling in an accessory building unless approved as an additional or accessory dwelling unit by Board of Adjustment special exception (51A-4.209(b)(6)(E)). An explicit shed-occupancy ban was not read.
shed.evidence: 51A-4.209(b)(6)(E)(i)-(iii): extra dwelling units only by BOA special exception.

tent.value: Campgrounds (RVs, tents, manufactured homes for temporary camping) are allowed by right only in the MH(A) district; tent living elsewhere is not a listed residential use.
tent.evidence: 51A-4.209(b)(4): manufactured home park/campground by right only in MH(A).

rv.value: RV occupancy is tied to campgrounds and transient stands, allowed only in MH(A); not a residential use on a single-family lot. No guest-stay allowance found in the code read.
rv.evidence: 51A-4.209(b)(4) campground definition, MH(A) only; 51A-2.102 transient stand definition.

thow.value: Not a listed dwelling type; RV-style units belong in campgrounds or manufactured home parks, allowed only in MH(A).

rooming.value: 'Lodging or boarding house' (1-5 separately rented guest rooms, no in-room kitchens) is by right only in MF-2(A), MF-2(SAH), MF-3(A), MF-4(A), RR, CS, LI, IR and central area; SUP in CR and IM. Not allowed in single-family districts.
rooming.evidence: 51A-4.205(2) Lodging or boarding house: definition and districts permitted.

coliving.value: Groups that are not a 'family' fall under 'group residential facility': by right in CH, multifamily, central area and mixed-use districts if 1,000 ft from others, otherwise SUP; not in single-family districts. SB 840 adds by-right multifamily on many commercial sites.
coliving.evidence: 51A-4.209(b)(3) group residential facility; SB 840 not re-read.

per_bedroom.value: Sec. 27-11 minimum property standards set owner duties but no per-occupant floor-area figure was found there; Ch. 27 Art. IV covers reducing occupancy load. Space-per-occupant rule not confirmed.
per_bedroom.evidence: Sec. 27-11 text searched: no square-feet-per-occupant standard.

permit.value: 2023 STR registration (Ch. 42B) and zoning ordinances are under a temporary injunction entered Dec 6, 2023; the city says it cannot enforce them meanwhile.
permit.evidence: Code Compliance STR page: injunction of 12/6/2023 bars enforcing both STR ordinances.

primary_residence.value: No owner-occupancy rule in force (2023 ordinances enjoined).
primary_residence.evidence: Injunction statement on city page; Ch. 42B text not read.

zones.value: 2023 zoning amendment allows 'short-term rental lodging' by right only in MO(A), GO(A), multifamily, central area, mixed use, multiple commercial and urban corridor districts (no single-family), but enforcement is enjoined.
zones.evidence: 51A-4.205(3) Short-term rental lodging districts; city page confirms injunction.

caps.value: Zoning text limits one STR per rentable unit; no other cap in force while the injunction stands.

max_occupancy.value: Codified Ch. 42B (enjoined, not enforced while the injunction stands): max three people per bedroom and 12 in total, two-night minimum stay, guest cars limited to off-street spaces.
max_occupancy.evidence: Dallas Code 42B-12(a) occupancy 3 per bedroom, total 12; 42B-12(e),(f). Injunction status from city STR page.

hostel_shared.value: Ch. 42B (enjoined) covers a full or partial rentable unit with a kitchen, bathroom and bedroom, so room rentals count, but only one STR per rentable unit; no hostel/bed-based model. Multitenant buildings with 20 or fewer units get zero STRs.

taxes.value: Owner must collect the 9% city hotel occupancy tax and remit monthly; the city has no platform collection agreement. State HOT of 6% (Tax Code 156.052) also applies.
taxes.evidence: Controller STR HOT page: 9% of net room receipts, no Airbnb/VRBO agreement; Tax Code 156.052 six percent.

listing_id.value: Ch. 42B (enjoined) requires every listing or ad to show the Dallas STR registration number plus occupancy, sound, vehicle and parking limits and the two-night minimum; platforms may not take fees for unregistered STRs.
listing_id.evidence: 42B-12(g)(1)-(6) listing contents; 42B-14(a) platform fee ban for unregistered units.

family.value: 'Family' means people living as one housekeeping unit with no more than four unrelated to the head of household (Dev. Code 51A-2.102).
family.evidence: 51A-2.102 FAMILY definition: not more than four unrelated individuals.

worship_zoning.value: Religious Assembly is permitted by right in every residential district (LA through MH) and most commercial and industrial districts; conditional only in CR and L. Housing on church land still follows the district's residential use and site rules.
worship_zoning.evidence: LDC 25-2-491 use table, row 'Religious Assembly'; 25-2-6 civic use definition.

shed.value: No zoning use makes a shed a dwelling; living space in an outbuilding must be a permitted dwelling unit (HOME rules allow up to three units on a lot under 25-2-773). No explicit shed-living ban was read.
shed.evidence: LDC 25-2-3 residential uses; 25-2-773 (title) two- and three-unit residential.

tent.value: Campgrounds are a commercial use (conditional in CR; permitted in CS, CS-1, CH, LI and some others), not allowed in residential zones; no explicit ban on a tent on a private lot was read.

rv.value: RV living quarters are framed as RV-park use (25-2-1261); an explicit ban on living in an RV on a residential lot was not found in the text read.

thow.value: Mobile homes may only be placed or occupied in licensed mobile home parks or subdivisions; RVs used as living quarters belong in RV parks. Tiny-home communities not confirmed.
thow.evidence: 25-2-1207(A) mobile home location; 25-2-1261 RV park definition.

rooming.value: Austin has no separate rooming-house use: boarding houses, dorms and fraternities fall under Group Residential (16+ adults with food provided by a third party), allowed in MF-4, MF-5, MF-6, CBD, DMU and CH, conditional in MF-3 and L, barred in single-family zones.
rooming.evidence: LDC 25-2-3 Group Residential definition; 25-2-491 table row 'Group Residential'.

coliving.value: No unrelated-adult cap since Dec 2023, so shared houses are ordinary residential use; SB 840 adds by-right multifamily on many commercial sites.

per_bedroom.value: No STR bedroom-based cap in current code: LDC 25-2-788 to 25-2-799 (old STR rules) were repealed and Ch. 4-23 has no occupancy limit. General property maintenance code applies (edition not checked).
per_bedroom.evidence: Editor's note: 25-2-788 to 25-2-799 STR sections repealed; Ch. 4-23 has no adult/bedroom limit.

permit.value: Yes: operator licence (Ch. 4-23), valid two years.
permit.evidence: City STR page: two-year licences since Oct 2025.

primary_residence.value: No (since 2025); tenants may operate with the landlord's consent.

zones.value: Accessory to any residential use in all base, special purpose, combining and overlay districts; cannot be prohibited (LDC 25-2-904).

caps.value: Up to 2 STRs per site of 3 or fewer units; other sites 1,000 ft apart; greater of 1 unit or 10% (4+ units, no commercial) or 25% (with commercial).

max_occupancy.value: No STR occupancy cap in current Ch. 4-23 or LDC 25-2-904; the old 25-2-795 limit was repealed.
max_occupancy.evidence: Ch. 4-23 full text has no occupancy cap; LDC 25-2-904 sets accessory use only.

hostel_shared.value: Partial-unit STRs allowed: the guest must get exclusive use of a bedroom and shared use of a full bathroom (4-23-34(C)).

taxes.value: Hotel occupancy tax, collected by platforms, with quarterly owner reports.

listing_id.value: Yes: operator must show licence number on ads; platforms must require it (from July 1, 2026).

pending.value: No pending rule change found; the city moves licensing to a new system Dec 4, 2026 (applications, renewals and HOT payments paused Nov 16 to Dec 3).

registration.value: Rental registration only for problem properties (Repeat Offender Program): triggered by repeat code violation notices or citations within 24 months; owner-occupied units exempt (City Code 4-14-3).

family.value: No zoning cap on unrelated occupants: the dwelling-unit occupancy limit (LDC 25-2-511) was repealed effective Dec 18, 2023 (Ord. 20231207-001).
family.evidence: 25-2-511 Reserved; editor's note on repeal of occupancy limit.

Cities may not run their own rental registration or licensing.
registration.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1902(A)-(C),(G); 9-1304(B)-(C); Maricopa Assessor Rental Registration page.

family.value: Family = any number of related persons (blood, marriage, adoption) plus servants, or up to five unrelated persons, living as one housekeeping unit.
family.evidence: Phoenix Zoning Ordinance Sec. 202 'Family' definitions 1 and 2.

per_bedroom.value: Floor-area rule, not per bedroom: at least 250 sq ft of gross dwelling area for the first two occupants and 150 sq ft per additional occupant; children under 13 excluded.
per_bedroom.evidence: Neighborhood Preservation Ordinance 39-5(E) Space and occupancy standards.

adu.value: Two ADUs allowed with one single-family home (one attached, one detached), a third if one is affordable on a lot of 1 acre+. Size: up to 75% of the house and 1,000 sq ft (lots over 10,000 sq ft: lesser of 3,000 sq ft or 10% of lot). Setbacks 3 ft side/rear. State mandate A.R.S. 9-461.18 applies.
adu.evidence: ZO 608 note 2 (two ADUs, third affordable); ZO 706.A.2-8; A.R.S. 9-461.18(A),(B).

shed.value: Accessory structures that are not ADUs have their own setbacks and height limits; living space must meet ADU rules (own sleeping and sanitation, Sec. 706.A). No specific shed-occupancy ban read.
shed.evidence: ZO 706.A vs 706.B accessory structures; ZO 202 ADU definitions.

tent.value: No explicit private-lot tent rule found. RV parks are the zoning use for tents and similar temporary living quarters, and a tent is not a listed dwelling in residential districts.
tent.evidence: ZO 202 'Recreational Vehicle Park' definition (tents included); 608 residential use table.

rv.value: Occupied RVs must be in a recreational vehicle park (C-1 to C-3 by special permit, max 20 spaces/acre), except hospital parking; a mobile home may be lived in during home construction only by use permit for up to one year.
rv.evidence: ZO 701 item 8 occupied RV in RV park; 647.A.2.g RV parks.

thow.value: 'Park model' (up to 400 sq ft, on wheels, ANSI) expressly includes tiny homes and is treated with RVs, so a wheeled tiny home is lived in only in an RV park; a tiny home on a foundation can be an ADU.
thow.evidence: ZO 202 'Park Model' and 'Recreational Vehicle Park' definitions; ZO 701 item 8.

rooming.value: Rooming house = group home. Boarding house (6+ unrelated lodgers paying per room) is not allowed in single-family districts; use permit in multifamily districts, 1,320 ft spacing, 25% lot coverage, 100 sq ft open space per bed, arterial/collector access.
rooming.evidence: ZO 202 'Boarding House', 'Rooming House'; ZO 608 use table and note 9.

coliving.value: Up to five unrelated adults may share a unit as a family; six or more is a boarding house or group home needing a use permit in multifamily zones. A.R.S. 9-462.13 middle-housing mandate (duplex-fourplex near downtown) applies to Phoenix.
coliving.evidence: ZO 202 Family; ZO 608 notes 9 and 18; A.R.S. 9-462.13(A); Phoenix implementing text not read.

hoa_data.value: No state HOA registry. Phoenix keeps a registry of HOAs and neighbourhood associations (STR owners must notify those within 600 ft); declarations are recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder.
hoa_data.evidence: Phoenix 10-199(E) HOAs registered with Neighborhood Services; registry itself not downloaded.

worship_zoning.value: 'Church/Place of Worship' is permitted by right in every residential district; accessory uses allowed with conditions. Religious assembly may include rectory, dormitory, school and day care. Housing beyond that needs the district's residential rules.
worship_zoning.evidence: ZO 608 use table row Church/Place of Worship 'p' all districts; ZO 202 'Religious Assembly'.

deposit.value: Cap of 1.5 months' rent for all security and prepaid rent (tenant may voluntarily prepay more). Within 14 days, excluding weekends and holidays, after move-out and tenant demand, landlord must send itemized deductions and refund; wrongful withholding risks twice the amount withheld.
deposit.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1321(A) 1.5-month cap; (D) 14 business days itemized list; (E) double damages.

notice.value: Month-to-month: written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice; week-to-week: 10 days. Either side may give it.
notice.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1375(A) week-to-week 10 days; (B) month-to-month 30 days before periodic rental date.

rluipa.value: Federal law: zoning may not substantially burden religious exercise without a compelling reason, must treat religious assemblies on equal terms with secular ones, and may not exclude them outright.
rluipa.evidence: Federal field already verified; not re-read in this AZ lane.

yigby.value: No YIGBY law. HB 2815 (2024) and HB 2191 (2025, single-family homes on church land) did not become law; SB 1096 (2026, senior living on religious sites) was prefiled. Current A.R.S. 9-462.15 is an unrelated assisted-living section, so church-land housing needs normal zoning.
yigby.evidence: Read SB1096 prefiled and HB2191 engrossed texts; Title 9 index has no religious-housing section; bill status pages not read.

hoa_law.value: Planned communities (ch. 16) and condos (ch. 9): owners may rent unless the declaration bans it and must follow its rental-period limits; HOA may only ask tenant names, contacts, lease dates, vehicles; $25 fee cap. Solar devices cannot be banned (33-1816). Listed flags and for-sale/rent signs protected (33-1808, 33-1261). Free records review in 10 business days (33-1805).

permit.value: Annual city vacation rental licence ($250) required since 8 Jan 2023, one per dwelling unit; issued within 7 business days. Needs TPT licence, 24-hour emergency contact, background attestations, $500,000 insurance (or platform cover) and written neighbour notice. Operating without one: fine of at least $1,000.

primary_residence.value: Not required, except an ADU with a certificate of occupancy issued on or after 14 Sep 2024 may be an STR only if the owner lives on the property as a primary residence. Restricted-affordable ADUs may never be STRs.

zones.value: Single-family dwellings 'including vacation rental or short-term rental' are permitted in residential districts; state law bars bans. Nonresidential uses (event centre, banquet, retail, sober living, adult business) prohibited.

caps.value: No numeric or density cap; state law preempts caps. A separate licence is needed for each house or dwelling unit.

max_occupancy.value: Required door notice states occupancy is limited to one family: one to six adults plus their related dependent children (zoning 'family' definition). With ADUs, the whole lot is capped at six adults.
max_occupancy.evidence: Code 18-175(h) notice item 9; Zoning Ord. 3.100 Family; 7.904.A.3.

hostel_shared.value: Not provided for. An STR is a dwelling rented under 30 days; lodging in non-dwelling buildings is 'travel accommodation' (commercial). Occupancy is capped at six adults, and minors may not rent.
hostel_shared.evidence: Zoning 3.100 'Vacation rental', 'Travel accommodation'; Code 18-178 juveniles; no hostel rule found.

taxes.value: State TPT licence required. Transient lodging: state+Maricopa County 7.27%, Scottsdale 1.7% plus 5% additional hotel/motel tax = about 13.97%. Platforms remit state/county tax for facilitated bookings.

listing_id.value: Yes. Every ad must list the city vacation rental licence number (minimum fine $500). Inside, post a laminated notice with licence number, local contact, banned uses and party rules, plus an egress/safety map.

pending.value: No pending litigation or vote found. Rules added: emergency contact must arrive in person within 1 hour (fines $250-$500), sex-offender check of booker 24 h before stays, juvenile rentals banned (2024), nuisance-party rules in Art. VIII.

registration.value: Owners of any residential rental must register with the Maricopa County Assessor; unregistered units may not be occupied; cities may fine but may not run their own rental registry or licence. STRs must also comply with assessor recording.

family.value: Family = one to six adults plus their related dependent children living as one housekeeping unit; state-licensed homes for people with developmental disabilities count as a family. 'Group home' = more than six adults sharing without care.

per_bedroom.value: No per-bedroom or floor-area occupancy rule found in the property maintenance article; the practical limit is the six-adult family definition (also lot-wide with ADUs).
per_bedroom.evidence: Code ch. 18 art. III searched; Zoning 3.100 Family; 7.904.A.3; building codes in ch. 31 not read.

adu.value: One attached and one detached ADU allowed on single-family lots (max two on lots under 1 acre; a third restricted-affordable one on 1 acre+). One may be 75% of the house or 1,000 sq ft, whichever less; others 500 sq ft. Separate meters, no separate sale; six adults total on the lot.

shed.value: A guest house is an accessory building for guests, not a dwelling: max half the house's floor area, no separate meter, never rented separately (deed restriction). Full-time living space needs an ADU approval.
shed.evidence: Table 5.102 note 6 guest house; Zoning 3.100 Guest house and ADU definitions.

tent.value: No tent-living rule found. Land may be used only for listed uses; residential tables list one main dwelling, ADUs and guest houses, not tents.
tent.evidence: Zoning Ord. 7.300 uses limited to those permitted; Table 5.102; no explicit tent text located.

rv.value: RVs are vehicles; no zoning use lets people live in one on a residential lot, and only listed uses are allowed. Specific RV-occupancy ban not located.
rv.evidence: Zoning 3.100 'Vehicle' includes campers and RVs; 7.300; Table 5.102.

thow.value: Not a listed dwelling type; a tiny home must meet ADU or dwelling rules (own sleeping, kitchen, sanitary facilities, building code). Wheeled units fall under vehicles.
thow.evidence: Zoning 3.100 'Dwelling unit', 'Accessory Dwelling Unit', 'Vehicle'; no tiny-home text.

rooming.value: 'Rooming house' points to 'boardinghouse', which has no definition in the current code, and group homes of more than six unrelated adults are not listed uses in single-family districts.
rooming.evidence: Zoning 3.100 'Rooming house. See boardinghouse'; Table 5.102 lacks group home.

coliving.value: Up to six unrelated adults may share a dwelling. Larger groups are 'group homes', not permitted in single-family districts. Middle housing mandate (A.R.S. 9-462.13) applies (Scottsdale over 75,000).
coliving.evidence: Zoning 3.100 Family, Group home; A.R.S. 9-462.13(A); local middle-housing text not read.

hoa_data.value: No state HOA registry; HOAs are usually Arizona nonprofit corporations (Corporation Commission filings) and declarations are recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder. No Scottsdale HOA list found.
hoa_data.evidence: Background; no registry dataset located this session.

worship_zoning.value: Place of worship permitted by right in single-family districts with standards: 20,000 sq ft minimum lot, FAR 0.20, 30 ft height (Design Review), collector-or-greater access, lights off 10 pm, no outdoor speakers. Permitted in commercial districts too.
worship_zoning.evidence: Table 5.102 row 18 and note 8; Art. XI commercial land use table.

str_preemption.value: No state preemption of STR rules found; cities license STRs (Minneapolis licence, Saint Paul Ch. 379). State and local taxes apply and facilitating platforms collect.
str_preemption.evidence: Negative finding; DOR residential STR guide plus city licence pages; statute search not exhaustive.

rent_control.value: Local rent control barred unless approved by voters at a general election (471.9996 subd. 2). Saint Paul has voter-approved rent stabilization (3% cap with exceptions).
rent_control.evidence: 471.9996 subd. 1 prohibition and subd. 2 general-election exception.

ltr_registration.value: No state rental registry; cities license (Minneapolis tiered rental licence, Saint Paul Fire C of O).
ltr_registration.evidence: Negative finding for state; city programs confirmed on city pages.

source_of_income.value: Status regarding public assistance, including rental assistance or rent supplements (vouchers), is a protected class in housing statewide.

occupancy_law.value: No statewide family-size rule, but licensed residential facilities for 6 or fewer and licensed day care up to 12 (group family day care 14) count as permitted single-family uses (462.357 subd. 7).

hoa_registry.value: No statewide HOA registry found; 515B associations must be incorporated (profit or nonprofit corporation), so SOS business filings and recorded plats/declarations are proxies.
hoa_registry.evidence: 515B.3-101 incorporation requirement; registry absence is a negative finding.

deposit.value: No statutory cap on amount. Return within three weeks after tenancy ends (5 days if condemned) with 1% simple annual interest, or give a written statement of amounts withheld.
deposit.evidence: 504B.178 subd. 2 (1% simple interest) and subd. 3 (three weeks, written statement); section sets no amount limit.

notice.value: Tenancy at will: written notice at least as long as the rent interval or three months, whichever is less (504B.135). Fixed-term and periodic leases follow their lease terms.
notice.evidence: 504B.135 Terminating tenancy at will: rent interval or three months, whichever less, in writing.

hoa_law.value: Common Interest Ownership Act (ch. 515B); association must keep records available to owners (515B.3-118). Flag bans void (500.215); solar limits restricted (500.216); child-care bans restricted (500.217). Use/occupancy (incl. leasing) restrictions must be in the declaration (515B.2-105(a)(11)).

yigby.value: SF 4915 (YIGBY Housing Act), companion HF 5020: introduced 3/26/2026, referred to Senate State and Local Government, no further action. Not law. Church-land housing needs normal zoning approval.
yigby.evidence: Spot-check: bill status shows introduction 3/26/2026 and committee referral only.

str_preemption.value: No state STR preemption statute found. Zaatari v. City of Austin (Tex. App.-Austin, Nov 27, 2019, No. 03-17-00812-CV) partly struck Austin's STR rules; review denied Jun 11, 2021. Dallas STR zoning ban is before the Texas Supreme Court (No. 25-0748).
str_preemption.evidence: Zaatari docket: 11/27/2019 affirmed in part, reversed/rendered in part; petition denied 6/11/2021.

rent_control.value: Cities may adopt rent control only after finding a disaster-caused housing emergency and with the governor's approval; it ends like a disaster declaration (Local Gov't Code 214.902).

ltr_registration.value: No state rental registry found. Dallas requires annual rental registration (Code 27-30, 27-31); Austin registers only repeat-offender properties (Code 4-14-3).
ltr_registration.evidence: City code sections read; absence of state registry not proven.

source_of_income.value: Cities and counties may not ban refusing tenants whose rent includes federal housing assistance (LGC 250.007); veteran protections and voluntary voucher incentives remain allowed.

occupancy_law.value: SB 840 (from 1 Sep 2025): large cities must allow multifamily/mixed-use by right on many commercial sites and conversions.

hoa_registry.value: Yes: TREC HOA management certificates (17,514 rows, name/county/city/ZIP, no geometry).

deposit.value: No statutory cap on amount; landlord must refund on or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the premises (Prop. Code 92.103).
deposit.evidence: Prop. Code 92.103(a): refund due by 30th day after surrender; no amount limit in Subch. C.

notice.value: Month-to-month: tenancy ends the later of the date in the notice or one month after notice; shorter rent periods use that period. A signed lease may set a different notice (Prop. Code 91.001).
notice.evidence: Prop. Code 91.001(a)-(e): one-month rule for monthly tenancies; lease can override.

hoa_law.value: Prop. Code ch. 209: certified-mail notice and cure before fines or suits (209.006), records access (209.005), open board meetings (209.0051), management certificate filed with county and TREC (209.004). Ch. 202 protects solar (202.010), rain barrels and drought landscaping (202.007), wind/hail-resistant shingles (202.011), flags (202.012), religious items (202.018), generators (202.019). Tarr (Tex. 2018) sided with owner on STR.
hoa_law.evidence: Read 202.007, 202.011, ch.202/209 headings, 209.004(b-1), 209.006; Tarr docket 16-1005: 5/25/2018 reversed for owner (opinion not read).

yigby.value: SB 854 (by-right housing on religious land) died in 2025. SB 840 (by-right multifamily on commercial land, from 1 Sep 2025) is the usable route.

str_preemption.value: No statewide STR preemption found; HB23-1287 (signed 2023) instead concerns county regulation of STRs. Home-rule cities such as Denver and Boulder license STRs themselves.
str_preemption.evidence: Bill search: HB23-1287 'County Regulation Related To Short-term Rentals' signed; bill text not read.

rent_control.value: Local rent control remains preempted (C.R.S. 38-12-301); HB23-1115, which would have repealed the ban, was lost in 2023.
rent_control.evidence: HB23-1115 status Lost; statute text not read (LexisNexis site requires accepting terms).

ltr_registration.value: No state rental registry found. Denver licenses all 30+ day rentals (2021 ordinance); Boulder requires a rental licence for every rental.
ltr_registration.evidence: Denver and Boulder licensing pages confirm local licences; absence of a state registry not provable from one page.

source_of_income.value: Protected statewide since HB20-1332: refusing to rent because of lawful source of income, including vouchers, is an unfair housing practice. Landlords with 3 or fewer units are exempt; owners of up to 5 single-family rentals need not accept federal vouchers for them.
source_of_income.evidence: HB20-1332 enacted summary: source of income made an unfair housing practice, with small-landlord exemptions.

occupancy_law.value: HB24-1007 (C.R.S. 29-20-111, effective Jul 1 2024) bars local limits on household size based on family relationship; limits allowed only from health/safety codes or affordable-housing rules. HB24-1152 makes subject jurisdictions allow one ADU by administrative approval wherever single-unit homes are allowed, from June 30 2025.
occupancy_law.evidence: HB24-1007 signed act adds 29-20-111(3); HB24-1152 summary section 1 ADU mandate.

hoa_registry.value: Yes: the Division of Real Estate publishes free HOA registration rosters (active and expired), with no map geometry; DRE says it cannot verify what HOAs report.
hoa_registry.evidence: DRE roster page lists HOA Active and Expired rosters, no fee; notes this is all it collects on HOAs.

deposit.value: Capped at two months' rent (C.R.S. 38-12-102.5, added by SB23-184, effective Aug 7 2023). From Jan 1 2027 the cap does not apply to post-closing occupancy agreements (SB26-054). Return within 1 month, or up to 60 days if the lease says so (38-12-103; timing not re-read).
deposit.evidence: SB23-184 signed act section 5 adds 38-12-102.5 two-month cap; SB26-054 summary adds post-closing exception.

notice.value: Notice to end a periodic tenancy (13-40-107 as amended by HB24-1098): 91 days (1 yr+), 28 (6-12 mo), 21 (1-6 mo), 3 (under 1 mo), 1 (under 1 wk). Most residential landlords also need cause (38-12-1303); nonpayment and lease-violation notices are 10 days; no-fault evictions need 90 days.
notice.evidence: HB24-1098 signed act sec. 5 rewrites 13-40-107(2); 38-12-1303 cause rule and 90-day no-fault notice.

hoa_law.value: CCIOA (C.R.S. 38-33.3). Section 38-33.3-106.5 voids HOA rules against flags and political signs, renewable-energy devices, drought-tolerant landscaping, child care and more; HB24-1152 added 106.5(4) voiding HOA ADU bans in ADU subject or supportive jurisdictions. Records access (38-33.3-317) and EV-charger rules not re-read.
hoa_law.evidence: HB24-1152 signed act sec. 6 adds 38-33.3-106.5(4); section heading lists the protected categories.

yigby.value: Enacted: HB26-1001 (signed Mar 25 2026) makes local governments over 2,000 people allow housing by administrative approval on parcels up to 5 acres owned by schools, colleges, housing authorities, transit districts or affordable-housing nonprofits, by Dec 31 2027. Church land qualifies through an agreement with such a nonprofit. HB25-1169 died May 2025.
yigby.evidence: HB26-1001 signed act, new 29-35-503 and definitions of qualifying entity and subject jurisdiction; HB25-1169 status Lost.

str_preemption.value: No statewide STR preemption enacted. HB 563 (134th GA, 2022) was reported from committee but never passed; later bills not checked.
str_preemption.evidence: HB 563 status page: introduced, referred, reported May 2022; no further action.

rent_control.value: Expressly preempted: R.C. 5321.19 bars local rent control or rent stabilization on private rentals (exceptions for city-owned housing and voluntary incentive agreements).
rent_control.evidence: R.C. 5321.19(A) prohibits political subdivisions from imposing rent control or stabilization.

ltr_registration.value: Owners of residential rental property must file owner/agent contact and parcel info with the county auditor and update within 60 days of changes (R.C. 5323.02).
ltr_registration.evidence: R.C. 5323.02(A),(C) filing with county auditor; updates within 60 days.

source_of_income.value: No statewide protection. Ohio fair-housing law covers race, color, religion, sex, military status, familial status, ancestry, disability, national origin; not source of income.
source_of_income.evidence: R.C. 4112.02(H) protected-class list omits source of income.

occupancy_law.value: No statewide family-definition or occupancy cap found; left to local zoning/housing codes.
occupancy_law.evidence: Negative finding; no specific statute located.

hoa_registry.value: No statewide HOA registry found in ORC 5312.
hoa_registry.evidence: Chapter 5312 section list has no registration provision.

deposit.value: No statutory cap. Itemized return within 30 days after move-out and delivery of possession. If held 6+ months, 5% yearly interest on the part above the greater of $50 or one month's rent.
deposit.evidence: R.C. 5321.16(A)-(B): interest on excess over $50 or one month's rent at 5%; itemized notice within 30 days; no cap stated.

notice.value: 30 days before the periodic rent date for month-to-month; 7 days for week-to-week (R.C. 5321.17).
notice.evidence: R.C. 5321.17(A)-(B) termination notice periods.

hoa_law.value: ORC 5312 (planned communities) / 5311 (condos): enforcement charges only after written notice and a hearing if requested; owners may inspect records. Solar devices allowed unless the declaration specifically bans them (5312.16/5311.192), with reasonable HOA limits. Condo flag display protected (5311.191).
hoa_law.evidence: R.C. 5312.11(C)-(D) notice/hearing; 5312.07 records; 5312.16 solar; 5311.191 condo flag display.

yigby.value: No state YIGBY law found.
yigby.evidence: Negative finding; no statute located in this pass.

str_preemption.value: None found: the Title 11 (municipal) index has no STR section; cities such as Tulsa license STRs directly.
str_preemption.evidence: Title 11 index searched; absence not proven.

rent_control.value: Preempted: no city may enact or enforce rent limits on private residential or commercial rentals; exceptions for city-owned, subsidized-by-agreement and CDBG-assisted property (11 O.S. 14-101.1).

ltr_registration.value: No state rental registry found. The Residential Landlord and Tenant Act only makes landlords disclose to tenants who owns and manages the unit and who accepts service (41 O.S. 116); Tulsa has only a vacant-building registry.
ltr_registration.evidence: Title 41 index: Residential Landlord and Tenant Act 101-136, 201; no registration section; 116 owner/manager identity disclosure.

source_of_income.value: No standalone protection. State housing law only bars refusing public assistance, alimony or child support as income when done because of a protected class (25 O.S. 1452(A)(8)).

occupancy_law.value: No statewide occupancy cap or family definition found: the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act lets landlords set use and occupancy rules (41 O.S. 126) but sets no persons-per-room limit; caps come from local zoning and property maintenance codes.
occupancy_law.evidence: Title 41 index: 126 tenant's use and occupancy - rules; no occupancy-limit section.

hoa_registry.value: No statewide HOA registry found; Real Estate Development Act (60 O.S. 851-858) shows no registration duty in its section list.

deposit.value: No statutory cap; deposit kept in an Oklahoma escrow account; balance returned within 45 days after tenancy ends, possession is delivered and the tenant makes written demand; unclaimed after 6 months it reverts to the landlord (41 O.S. 115).
deposit.evidence: 41 O.S. 115(A)-(B): escrow, 45-day return after written demand, 6-month reversion.

notice.value: Month-to-month or at-will: 30 days' written notice; tenancy shorter than month-to-month: 7 days (41 O.S. 111).

hoa_law.value: Condos: Unit Ownership Estate Act (60 O.S. 501+). Real Estate Development Act (60 O.S. 851-858) covers owners associations and covenant copies; 60 O.S. 858 bars associations from blocking a US flag up to 20 ft. No solar protection found.
hoa_law.evidence: Title 60 index ch. 11 and ch. 17; 60 O.S. 858 text read.

yigby.value: No state law allowing housing by right on religious or institutional land found; the only overlay is federal RLUIPA. A full-text OSCN statute search was not run.
yigby.evidence: Negative finding; OSCN Title 11 index has no faith-based housing section; federal RLUIPA only.

str_preemption.value: No state STR preemption law: an official statute search for 'short-term rental' returns only an unrelated tax section (RSMo 137.018). Pending bills not checked.
str_preemption.evidence: Revisor full-text search: one match, 137.018 (ad valorem merchandise exemption).

rent_control.value: Preempted: no city or county may regulate rent on private residential or commercial property (RSMo 441.043.1). 2025 amendments (H.B. 595) also bar local source-of-income, screening-criteria, deposit-limit and right-of-first-refusal ordinances.
rent_control.evidence: RSMo 441.043.1 and .2, as amended by 2025 H.B. 595 & 343, effective Aug 28 2025.

ltr_registration.value: No state rental registry found. Kansas City requires a Healthy Rental Homes permit for rentals of 30+ days (Code ch. 34, art. XIX).
ltr_registration.evidence: KCMO Sec. 34-832 rental permit; state-level absence not provable from one page.

source_of_income.value: No statewide protection, and since Aug 28 2025 cities and counties may not bar landlords from refusing tenants whose rent includes housing assistance (RSMo 441.043.2(1)); local bans on veterans'-benefits discrimination remain allowed.
source_of_income.evidence: RSMo 441.043.2(1) and .4, as amended by 2025 H.B. 595.

occupancy_law.value: RSMo 441.060.2: a limit of two persons per bedroom is presumed reasonable statewide; children born to the tenants during the lease are excepted.

hoa_registry.value: No statewide HOA registry found; HOAs appear only as Secretary of State nonprofit entities.
hoa_registry.evidence: No registration duty found in 442.404 or revisor searches; SOS proxy not re-checked.

deposit.value: Capped at two months' rent; return it or an itemized list within 30 days after the tenancy ends (RSMo 535.300). Since Aug 28 2025 cities and counties may not set their own deposit limits (RSMo 441.043.2(3)).
deposit.evidence: RSMo 535.300.1 cap and .3 thirty-day return; 441.043.2(3) bars local deposit limits.

notice.value: Month-to-month, at-will or under-one-year tenancies end with one month's written notice (RSMo 441.060.1 and .4).
notice.evidence: RSMo 441.060.1 and .4 one month's written notice; source URL corrected from 441.043.

hoa_law.value: RSMo 442.404: HOA covenants may not ban political signs, solar panels (reasonable placement rules allowed) or for-sale signs, and the section also covers chicken-keeping; condos fall under ch. 448.
hoa_law.evidence: RSMo 442.404 heading and subsections on signs, solar, sale signs, chickens; condo associations excluded.

yigby.value: No Missouri statute allowing by-right housing on faith or institutional land found in official statute searches.
yigby.evidence: Revisor search 'religious' + 'dwelling' returned only tax, urban renewal and fair-housing sections.

str_preemption.value: No STR preemption found; cities regulate via zoning and business licences. State lodging tax (Ala. Code 40-26-1) covers stays under 180 days: 5% in Madison and other mountain-lakes counties, 4% elsewhere. Platform collection not confirmed.
str_preemption.evidence: Ala. Code 40-26-1(a)-(b) rates and 180-day exclusion; no preemption statute located.

rent_control.value: Preempted: local governments may not enact or enforce rules controlling rent on private property (Ala. Code 11-80-8.1).

source_of_income.value: None. Alabama Fair Housing Law covers race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin (and handicap); not source of income.

hoa_registry.evidence: Negative finding; Act 35-20 sections read contain no registry.

deposit.value: Capped at one month's rent, except extra for pets, alterations or added liability risk. Refund or itemized list within 60 days after move-out; missing the deadline costs double the deposit.

notice.value: Month-to-month: written notice 30 days before the periodic rent date; week-to-week: 7 days (Ala. Code 35-9A-441).
notice.evidence: Ala. Code 35-9A-441(a)-(b).

hoa_law.value: Homeowners' Association Act (Ala. Code 35-20) applies to HOA declarations recorded on/after Jan 1 2016, or older HOAs that opt in by majority; not condos (35-8/8A). Solar/flag protections not confirmed.
hoa_law.evidence: Ala. Code 35-20-3 applicability; 35-20-2 definitions. Solar/flag not checked.

yigby.value: No state YIGBY law found.

str_preemption.value: Cities and counties may not ban STRs or regulate them by classification, use or occupancy. They may require a permit (max $250, decision in 7 business days), emergency contact, neighbour notice, licence number on ads, $500,000 insurance, owner residence only for post-9/14/2024 ADUs; fines $500-$3,500 and suspensions up to 12 months.
str_preemption.evidence: A.R.S. 9-500.39(A)-(G),(K); 11-269.17 county twin listed in Title 11 index (not read).

rent_control.value: Rent control on private residential property is preempted statewide; cities, including charter cities, may not control rents. Exception: housing owned, financed, insured or subsidised by state or local government.

deposit.value: Cap of 1.5 months' rent for all security and prepaid rent (tenant may voluntarily prepay more). Within 14 days, excluding weekends and holidays, after move-out and tenant demand, landlord must send itemized deductions and refund; wrongful withholding risks twice the amount withheld.
deposit.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1321(A) 1.5-month cap; (D) 14 business days itemized list; (E) double damages.

notice.value: Month-to-month: written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice; week-to-week: 10 days. Either side may give it.
notice.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1375(A) week-to-week 10 days; (B) month-to-month 30 days before periodic rental date.

ltr_registration.value: Yes, via county assessor: every residential rental owner must keep owner, parcel and year-built data with the assessor (out-of-state owners name an in-state agent; fee max $10); unregistered rentals may not be occupied. Cities and counties may not adopt their own rental registration or licensing.

source_of_income.value: State fair housing law does not list source of income. No state preemption found; Phoenix protects source of income (incl. vouchers) by city ordinance since 2023, Scottsdale does not.
source_of_income.evidence: A.R.S. 41-1491.14 protected classes; Phoenix Code 18-11 et seq. (Ord. G-7086); preemption search not exhaustive.

occupancy_law.value: Cities over 75,000 must allow one attached and one detached ADU by right, rentable long-term, no owner-occupancy or parking rules (9-461.18); duplex-fourplex/townhomes near downtown (9-462.13); housing on obsolete commercial sites in cities 150,000+ (9-462.10). Assisted living homes of 10 or fewer cannot be capped (9-462.15).

hoa_law.value: Planned communities (ch. 16) and condos (ch. 9): owners may rent unless the declaration bans it and must follow its rental-period limits; HOA may only ask tenant names, contacts, lease dates, vehicles; $25 fee cap. Solar devices cannot be banned (33-1816). Listed flags and for-sale/rent signs protected (33-1808, 33-1261). Free records review in 10 business days (33-1805).

hoa_registry.value: No statewide HOA registry found. Associations are typically nonprofit corporations filed with the Arizona Corporation Commission; declarations are recorded by county recorders. Owners must get free records access within 10 business days.
hoa_registry.evidence: Negative finding; A.R.S. 33-1805(A) records access read.

yigby.value: No YIGBY law. HB 2815 (2024) and HB 2191 (2025, single-family homes on church land) did not become law; SB 1096 (2026, senior living on religious sites) was prefiled. Current A.R.S. 9-462.15 is an unrelated assisted-living section, so church-land housing needs normal zoning.
yigby.evidence: Read SB1096 prefiled and HB2191 engrossed texts; Title 9 index has no religious-housing section; bill status pages not read.

items.value: Listing types are entire place, room (private bedroom) and shared room (bedroom or common area possibly shared with others). The help article does not limit shared rooms to staffed hostels.
items.evidence: Article 317 Select your home type: Entire place, Room, Shared room definitions; no hostel or 24/7 staff rule.

items.value: Community Disturbance Policy: no disruptive or open-invite gatherings or party-friendly ads; Airbnb may block higher-risk bookings and warn, suspend or remove listings or accounts.
items.evidence: Article 3345 sections What's not allowed, Reducing, Enforcing.

items.value: Smoke and CO alarms strongly urged; hosts record safety devices in the listing; local rules may require more alarms. Free combo alarm for eligible hosts.
items.evidence: Spot-check: article 514 alarms guidance and update-safety-device steps.

items.value: US responsible-hosting guidance: set safe occupancy limits, check local permits, zoning, taxes and safety rules, keep smoke/CO alarms, no indoor cameras. Guidance only; no per-bed or registration-field rule here.
items.evidence: Article 1376 Safety, Occupancy, General regulations sections.

items.value: Partners are responsible for local licensing, permits, zoning, safety and tax; licence/registration fields appear where a place requires them.

Property type is chosen at registration and cannot be changed later: Apartment, Home (entire place) or Hotel, where Hotel covers motels, hostels, resorts and lodges with shared areas. Hostel beds sell individually (a bunk counts as two single beds); vacation homes rent only whole, guest houses only per room.
items.evidence: Partner Help 'Registering your property step-by-step': Choosing your property type; Hostel bunk-bed rule; layout per property type.

items.value: Registration/permit numbers go in a dedicated field (Local laws > Regulatory Compliance), preferred over the description; multiple numbers comma-separated.
items.evidence: Help article steps: Local laws, Regulatory Compliance, Edit registration; recommends dedicated field; comma-separate multiple numbers.
